test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Feb, 2026 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
In the given figure, angle ABC = 70^circ . Angle AEF = 50^circ . Angle CDE = 45^circ . What is the value (in degrees) of angle ACD ?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/187c8da7a31e570eb36ad3f76e9bd9fbf334dbff2a61d46505290470cc85e7ca.png]
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In ΔFBD, Exterior ∠AFE = ∠ABC + ∠CDE = 70° + 45° = 115°.

In ΔAFE, ∠FAE = 180° − (∠AFE + ∠AEF) = 180° − (115° + 50°) = 15°.

In ΔABC, Exterior ∠ACD = ∠ABC + ∠BAC = 70° + 15° = 85°.

**∴ The correct answer is 85°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ∠ABC = 70°, ∠AEF = 50°, ∠CDE = 45°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36897dd04776a00a6c9f64a5fa5b87ba85f05881c95eab5777de200ce16390fc.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Exterior Angle Theorem: The exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles.

Sum of interior angles of a triangle = 180°.

**Calculations:**

⇒ In ΔFBD, ∠AFE is the exterior angle at vertex F.

⇒ ∠AFE = ∠FBD + ∠FDB

⇒ ∠AFE = 70° + 45° = 115°

⇒ Now, in ΔAFE, the sum of angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠FAE + ∠AFE + ∠AEF = 180°

⇒ ∠FAE + 115° + 50° = 180°

⇒ ∠FAE = 180° − 165° = 15°

⇒ Since A, E, C are collinear, ∠BAC = ∠FAE = 15°.

⇒ In ΔABC, ∠ACD is the exterior angle at vertex C.

⇒ ∠ACD = ∠ABC + ∠BAC

⇒ ∠ACD = 70° + 15° = 85°

**∴ The correct answer is 85°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

An exterior angle of a triangle is formed by extending one of its sides. It is always equal to the sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles (∠ext = ∠int1 + ∠int2).

Angle Sum Property

For any triangle, the sum of all three interior angles is constant and equal to 180°.

Vertically Opposite Angles

When two lines intersect, the angles opposite each other are equal. In this problem, ∠AEF and ∠CED are not necessarily vertically opposite unless F-E-D and A-E-C are both straight lines intersecting at E.
